meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_215_packages.json, all reference===215 edges from torahData.js (2 found, both eitza: IDs 629 and 2095), and the full source text torah_215.txt. For each statement in the source text, evaluated whether it employs explicit bechina language (בְּחִינַת, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת, נִקְרָא, הוּא בְּחִינַת, הִיא) or an equivalent structural bechina (gematria midpoint as essential identity). Only statements with explicit bechina declarations or clearly structural bechina identity claims are proposed as missing edges. Causal/sequential statements using עַל-יְדֵי, וְעַל-כֵּן, בָּזֶה are classified as eitza. All proposed edges are confirmed absent from torahData.js for reference 215.

additions.description: עֵת רָצוֹן is a bechina of הִתְגַּלּוּת מֵצַח הָרָצוֹן
additions.source_quote: וּלְזֶה הַפִּדְיוֹן צָרִיךְ עֵת רָצוֹן, בְּחִינַת הִתְגַּלּוּת מֵצַח הָרָצוֹן
additions.notes: The Rebbe explicitly uses 'בְּחִינַת' to declare that eit ratzon is a bechina of 'the revelation of the forehead of will.' The metzach (forehead) in Kabbalistic thought (Zohar, Idra Rabba) is the location of divine ratzon — at the 'forehead' of Arich Anpin (the attribute of infinite will), divine favor radiates and harsh judgments (dinim) are sweetened. Eit ratzon — the moment when this forehead-will is revealed — is therefore not merely caused by the metzach haratzon but IS it: the moment of eit ratzon is the moment of metzach haratzon's revelation. They are two names for the same spiritual event. This is the load-bearing bechina of the entire Torah: the universal redemption works precisely because it requires and accesses this specific supernal dimension.

additions.description: שַׁבָּת בְּמִנְחָה is a bechina of עֵת רָצוֹן
additions.source_quote: כְּמוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת בְּמִנְחָה, בְּחִינַת: וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּתִי וְכוּ', עֵת רָצוֹן וְכוּ'
additions.notes: The Rebbe gives Shabbat Mincha as the prime example of eit ratzon using explicit 'בְּחִינַת' language. The proof-verse is Psalms 69:14: 'וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּתִי לְךָ ה' עֵת רָצוֹן' (But as for me, my prayer is to You, O Lord, at an acceptable time). Shabbat Mincha is traditionally identified as the time of exceptional divine favor — the time of Mincha Gedolah or Mincha of Shabbat afternoon, when the third Shabbat meal is eaten and the Rebbe Nachman corpus repeatedly identifies it as the time of special closeness. Moses also died at this time (Shabbat Mincha), and this is not coincidental — his death was timed to align with eit ratzon in order to perform the universal sweetening described in the teaching. The bechina here is: Shabbat Mincha IS eit ratzon — not merely a time that has eit ratzon, but the temporal-liturgical embodiment of it.

additions.description: מֹשֶׁה is a bechina of the mediator between שְׁמָד and רָצוֹן (gematria midpoint)
additions.source_quote: מֹשֶׁה עוֹמֵד בֵּין שְׁמָד לְרָצוֹן, כִּי מִסְפַּר מֹשֶׁה הוּא מְמֻצָּע בֵּין מִסְפַּר שְׁמָד לְמִסְפַּר רָצוֹן
additions.notes: The Rebbe establishes Moses' essential identity via gematria: מֹשֶׁה = 345, שְׁמָד = 344, רָצוֹן = 346. Moses IS the numerical midpoint — not approximately, but exactly. The Rebbe uses 'מְמֻצָּע' (midpoint/average) — a precise mathematical and ontological claim. This is a bechina declaration using gematria as the proof of essential parallel nature. Moses' very name encodes his cosmic function: to stand between the forces of coercion/destruction (shemad = forced apostasy, persecution) and divine will/favor (ratzon). This is not a cause-effect statement (that would be: 'because Moses has this gematria, he can sweeten shemad') — it is an identity statement: Moses' nature IS this mediation. Gematria-based bechina is a well-established form of bechina declaration in Rebbe Nachman's Torahs. The edge proposed here connects מֹשֶׁה and שְׁמָד as the two poles of Moses' identity; a companion edge connecting מֹשֶׁה and רָצוֹן is proposed separately (see next entry).

additions.description: מֹשֶׁה is a bechina of רָצוֹן (gematria midpoint — other pole)
additions.source_quote: מֹשֶׁה עוֹמֵד בֵּין שְׁמָד לְרָצוֹן, כִּי מִסְפַּר מֹשֶׁה הוּא מְמֻצָּע בֵּין מִסְפַּר שְׁמָד לְמִסְפַּר רָצוֹן
additions.notes: Companion to the previous entry. The same gematria declaration establishes Moses' relationship to both poles simultaneously: שְׁמָד (344) — מֹשֶׁה (345) — רָצוֹן (346). Moses is adjacent to ratzon just as he is adjacent to shemad. This bechina edge captures the positive pole: Moses' essence partakes of ratzon (will/divine favor) as much as it mediates shemad. This is why his death at Shabbat Mincha (= eit ratzon = Package 1) is the ultimate act of his mission — he dies at the moment that IS ratzon in order to complete the sweetening. Note on potential node alias: this 'רָצוֹן' node (standalone will) may be aliased with 'עֵת רָצוֹן' from Package 1 — both refer to the reality of divine ratzon, but 'עֵת רָצוֹן' is the temporal manifestation while 'רָצוֹן' is the abstract quality. In Rebbe Nachman's teachings these often function as a single node. The dataset maintainer may wish to resolve this alias question when adding these edges.

additions.description: עַכּוּ"ם and חֲרוֹן אַף are bechina equivalents (parallel presence in the world)
additions.source_quote: כִּי כָּל זְמַן שֶׁיֵּשׁ עַכּוּ"ם בָּעוֹלָם חֲרוֹן אַף בָּעוֹלָם
additions.notes: The Rebbe cites a rabbinic dictum (indicated by the parenthetical 'ב' = second reference, a traditional citation marker): 'כָּל זְמַן שֶׁיֵּשׁ עַכּוּ"ם בָּעוֹלָם חֲרוֹן אַף בָּעוֹלָם' — whenever there are idol worshippers in the world, there is divine wrath in the world. The syntactic structure — 'כָּל זְמַן שֶׁ...X בָּעוֹלָם, Y בָּעוֹלָם' — establishes these as ontologically inseparable presences. This is not a causal statement (idol worshippers do not merely cause wrath; rather, their presence IS the presence of wrath — they are two faces of the same negative reality). The Rebbe uses this to explain why the heavenly realm uses the sweetening for making converts: because the sweetening of the judgment (the 24 courts) IS the sweetening of the wrath, which IS the transformation of the idol-worshippers into converts. The three things are bechina-parallel: judgment/court → charon af → akum. The edge here captures the most explicit leg of this equation. The bechina classification is confirmed by the sequel: 'וּכְשֶׁמַּמְתִּיקִין הַדִּין וְהַחֲרוֹן אַף, נִמְתָּק הָעַכּוּ"ם' — sweetening the judgment AND the charon af results in the akum being sweetened — all three are treated as variants of the same entity being transformed. Note: this edge has a lower priority than the Package 1 and Package 2 edges because the 'bechina' here is implicit (parallel existence) rather than explicitly marked with 'בְּחִינַת' language. However, the structural equivalence is strong and consistent with how the Rebbe uses such parallel-presence formulations elsewhere.

existing_eitza_edges.note: The redemption/sweetening → converts: causal/eitza correctly classified.
When judgment/wrath is sweetened → idol worshippers are sweetened and become converts: causal/eitza correctly classified.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: כ"ד פִּדְיוֹנוֹת / כ"ד בָּתֵּי דִּינִים (24 redemptions / 24 courts of judgment)
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: The 24 courts of judgment are introduced at the opening as a structural fact — they are not equated to each other or to another concept via bechina language. The Torah merely states 'there are 24 types of redemption because there are 24 courts of judgment' — this is a structural correspondence, not a bechina. The 24 courts are the domain of Package 3 (the evil/judgment cluster), but the number itself is not the subject of a bechina declaration. The count '24' corresponds to the 24 books of the Tanach, a well-known correspondence, but the Rebbe does not make that equation explicitly in this Torah. The 24 courts are included in Package 3 as contextual nodes but do not themselves generate a new bechina edge.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: חַד בְּדָרָא (the one unique individual in a generation)
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: The Rebbe states that only one individual per generation knows the universal redemption. This is a quantitative/functional description, not a bechina declaration. No bechina language ('הוּא בְּחִינַת', 'נִקְרָא', etc.) is applied to 'chad b'dara.' It characterizes the rarity of the knowledge; it is context for the eitza (why the redemption often fails to work) rather than an ontological equation between concepts.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: מוּל בֵּית פְּעוֹר (buried opposite Beth Peor)
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Moses' burial site (opposite Beth Peor, the location of idol worship) is cited as evidence that Moses continued his work of sweetening after death. This is a narrative/factual reference supporting an eitza argument (Moses' burial placement causes ongoing sweetening of akum). The Rebbe does not use bechina language to equate Beth Peor with any concept. It is a locational fact functioning as a proof-element in the eitza chain.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הַגָּדוֹל (Rabbi Eliezer the Great)
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Rabbi Eliezer is identified as a reincarnation (גִּלְגּוּל) of Moses' son Eliezer. The Rebbe uses this to explain Rabbi Eliezer's ability to make converts. However, the text does not declare 'Rabbi Eliezer IS a bechina of Moses' son Eliezer' using bechina language — it uses 'גִּלְגּוּל' (reincarnation) language. Reincarnation is a different category from bechina: it is a biographical-spiritual fact about souls, not an ontological equivalence of concepts. Excluded from bechina analysis. The statement about Rabbi Eliezer functions as a historical validation (eitza-level proof) of the teaching's claim about Moses' ongoing influence.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: יִתְרוֹ (Jethro) converting because he was Moses' father-in-law
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: The Rebbe explains Jethro's conversion by citing the verse 'וַיִּשְׁמַע יִתְרוֹ חוֹתֵן מֹשֶׁה' — Jethro heard because he was Moses' father-in-law. This is an eitza explanation: being Moses' father-in-law caused him to hear and convert. No bechina equation is being declared about Jethro as a concept. He is a historical example supporting the broader teaching about Moses' converts-making influence, not a concept being equated to another via bechina.

Moses' effort to bring the erev rav close is cited as evidence of his lifelong mission of making converts. The erev rav is mentioned as the object of Moses' outreach, not as a concept being equated to another via bechina language. The Rebbe does not declare 'הָעֵרֶב רַב הוּא בְּחִינַת X.' Excluded.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: בֶּן מֹשֶׁה / אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן מֹשֶׁה (Eliezer son of Moses)
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: The verse cited ('וְשֵׁם הָאֶחָד אֱלִיעֶזֶר') identifies Rabbi Eliezer the Great as the reincarnation of Moses' son Eliezer. While this is a bechina-like equation in substance, it uses the language of gilgul (reincarnation), not bechina. The Rebbe does not write 'רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הוּא בְּחִינַת אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן מֹשֶׁה' — he writes 'הָיָה גִּלְגּוּל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה.' Gilgul language is distinct from bechina language in the dataset's framework. Excluded from bechina edges.

structural_observations: Torah #215 is a compact but structurally dense teaching — 9 sentences covering the cosmology of redemption, the unique universal redemption, Moses' cosmic mission, and two historical validations (Rabbi Eliezer, Jethro).

The teaching has a three-package structure: (1) good: eit ratzon / metzach haratzon / Shabbat Mincha — the channel of universal sweetening; (2) good: Moses / shemad / ratzon — Moses as the cosmic mediator; (3) evil: akum / charon af / 24 courts — the domain being sweetened.

The two existing eitza edges in the dataset (IDs 629 and 2095) correctly capture the causal flow: sweetening → converts. What is entirely missing is the bechina backbone that explains WHY the sweetening works: (a) eit ratzon IS metzach haratzon IS Shabbat Mincha; (b) Moses IS the midpoint between shemad and ratzon; (c) akum IS charon af.

The Torah exhibits the classic good/evil mirror structure (framework section 4): Package 1 (ratzon/divine will) mirrors Package 3 (charon af/wrath); they are the same cosmic reality with opposite orientations — divine favor vs. divine wrath. Moses (Package 2) stands at the interface.

The gematria proof (Moses = 345, midpoint of shemad 344 and ratzon 346) is one of the most precise numerical bechina declarations in the Likutay Moharan. The three numbers are consecutive integers, making Moses literally the arithmetic median — not an approximation but an exact identity.

Moses dying on Shabbat Mincha functions as the narrative synthesis of the entire Torah: Package 2 (Moses) acts at Package 1 (Shabbat Mincha = eit ratzon) to transform Package 3 (akum/charon af) into גרים — the eitza result.
